purpose: Detect careless answering in pilot and public data, and measure within-session reliability. Quality flags never change anyone's results page; they decide which responses are used to calibrate the model.

instructed_responses.note: Three checks placed at random in the middle third of the quiz, each inside a different module and styled like the items around it. Each names the answer to pick, so nobody fails by disagreeing.

items.stem: This question checks that answers are being read. Please choose "About as much as today".
items.scope: There is no right opinion here; just pick the answer named above.

items.stem: To show you're reading carefully, please choose "Sometimes (about 3 in 10)" for this question.
items.scope: Just pick the answer named above.
options: Almost always (9 or more times in 10)

items.stem: Attention check: please choose "Lean" toward the side labeled "Blue".
items.scope: Just pick the answer named above.

repeated_items.note: Asked again at the very end, shown in the opposite display direction from the first time. Agreement between the two answers estimates within-session reliability and flags random responding. Chosen to span six different families of axes.
repeated_items.flag_if: Four or more of the six repeated answers differ from the first answer by 2 or more scale points (positions scaled to 0-1, difference >= 0.5).

timing_and_patterns.too_fast: Under 2 seconds on a position or tradeoff item, or under 1 second on an exception case. Flag the response if more than 30% of answered items are too fast.
timing_and_patterns.straightlining: The same on-screen position (first, last, etc.) chosen on 12 or more consecutive multi-option items. Because display direction is randomized per person, this pattern cannot come from consistent views.
timing_and_patterns.breakoff: Partial responses are kept; items answered before stopping count normally.

self_report.stem: Last question about the quiz itself: how carefully did you answer?
self_report.scope: Your honest answer helps us. It doesn't change your results.
options: Carefully and honestly, all or almost all the way through
Mostly carefully, with some quick guesses
I clicked through a lot of it without thinking

exclusion_rule: For calibration, exclude a response if it fails 2 or more of the 3 instructed checks, OR it is flagged for both speed and straightlining, OR the self-report is the third option. Report how many were excluded and rerun key results with them included, to show the rule doesn't drive conclusions.
